svg.title: Enhanced base change and compact generation by Koszul stages
svg.desc: The full multiplication adjunction tensors to the actual regular-algebra module category, which is the relative tensor of the automorphic category with its spectral coefficients. Continuous transpose lands in the full Hecke-lisse category. Both inverse identities identify that category with restricted spectral base change. Actual finite equivariant Koszul stages have continuous linear left and right adjoints and conservative relative pushforwards. Enhanced compact generators push to compact generators of the full Hecke-lisse category. Stage operators preserve regular inputs. Replacing the ambient compact generators by regular intrinsic point objects requires the separate point-detection hypothesis; only then does full-image regularity follow.
svg.text: Enhanced base change and compact generation by Koszul stages
Complex coefficients; every curve genus and reductive component; full unbounded categories.
1. The actual regular-algebra bar — ESG.1–ESG.5
K(T) = (Id ⊗ f*L)R(R), E(T) = Mod(K(T))(M ⊗ T).
Tensor the full multiplication adjunction, including its unit and counit.
E(T) ≃ (M ⊗ T) ⊗(R ⊗ R) R ≃ M ⊗R T.
The right adjoint is conservative; free objects and all action faces are retained.
2. Actual landing and both inverse identities — ESG.6–ESG.14
j = Id(M) ⊗R D = (Id(M) ⊗ Γ!) U(A), q = Id(M) ⊗R L.
Full enhanced eigen-comparison ⇒ j(E(A)) lies in N, the Hecke-lisse category.
qj ≃ Id, jq ≃ Π, Π restricted to N ≃ Id.
M ⊗R A ≃ N with its existing A-action; E(T) ≃ N ⊗A T.
Both inverse identities and full landing are required; a section alone is insufficient.
3. Finite equivariant Koszul stages — ESG.18–ESG.24
K(E) = B ⊗ᴸSym(W(E)) C, Z(E) = [Spec K(E) / H].
The actual rational equivariant lift retains every derived algebra map.
f* ⊣ f_* ⊣ f!, f!(a) = K(E) dual over B ⊗ᴸB a.
All three functors are continuous and A-linear; f_* is conservative.
The supported unit is C(S), not B. Both degree and character shifts remain.
4. Unconditional compact generation — ESG.25–ESG.31
Id(N) ⊗ f* ⊣ J(E,N) ⊣ Id(N) ⊗ f!.
J(E,N) preserves compact objects and forgets the actual K(E)-action.
P(E) ⊣ J(E), J(E) = inclusion ∘ J(E,N), continuous and conservative.
Compact generators c(α) of M give compact generators P(E)c(α) of E(T(E)).
{ J(E,N) P(E)c(α) : E, α } compactly generates the full N.
5. Regular inputs and the exact conditional implication — ESG.32–ESG.35
T(E) = J(E)P(E) preserves every chartwise ind-regular input.
The actual kernel parameters lie in original-complex ind-connections.
Additional hypothesis: original-complex extraordinary point fibres detect N.
Then P(E)δ(y)! generate every stage; their relative images are compact and regular.
Point detection on N ⇒ N lies in M(reg).
The Hecke-lisse/nilpotent support criterion is a separate required argument.
Exact proofs: §§3.264–3.278, ESG.1–ESG.45; Solutions3.EB,3.EC,3.ED.
Graph modules can make enhanced pushforward conservative even when invariants are not.
Stage monads need not be idempotent; coherent derived residues need not be compact.
Γ! on the whole restricted category and ordinary Γ on compact-unit stages are distinct.
No nilpotent support equality or unconditional point-detection statement is asserted.
